title: POC definition: SDK bridge, tool-calling, structured output specs with Lodestar Commerce
summary: Kickoff to define POC success criteria, workload sizing and benchmarks. Focus on integrating Redwood SDK and OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, and structured JSON outputs for Lodestar's commerce search and assistant. Agreed benchmarks for latency, throughput, quality thresholds and a 4-week sprint timeline with engineering checkpoints.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-16 16:00 UTC
Duration (mins): 58
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Lodestar Eng Mgr), Priya Natarajan (Lodestar ML), Marcus Cole (Lodestar Platform)

Auto-summary:
Short: Define POC success criteria and measurements. Focus on integrating Redwood SDK or OpenAI-compatible endpoints, tool/function-calling for order fulfillment intents, and structured JSON outputs for downstream systems. Agree next steps and owners.

[00:00:00] Alex (AE): Okay, hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call? say your name and role so we have it on the note.
[00:00:08] Jordan: Jordan Lee, engineering manager on search and conversational products here at Lodestar.
[00:00:12] Priya: Priya Natarajan, lead ML engineer—working the assistant and reranking pipeline.
[00:00:16] Marcus: Marcus Cole, platform infra, I own VPC and KMS stuff.
[00:00:20] Alex: Great, and from Redwood, Samir and I, Samir's our SE. We'll run through a proposed pilot scope.

[00:01:05] Samir (SE): Alright, quick agenda—success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, integration options (SDK vs OpenAI-compat), tool calling / function design, structured output, security, timeline. We'll pause for Q's after each section.

[00:02:12] Jordan: Sounds good. High-level our goal is to ship a conversational assistant that can do product lookup, order tracking, and generate structured fulfillment intents for backend systems. Success metrics are accuracy of intent extraction, latency under 400ms p50 and 800ms p95 for 99% of user-facing calls, and cost under $X per 1k requests—we'll need Redwood's help to quantify.

[00:03:45] Samir: Good, that's clear. Can you describe the expected request profile—tokens in prompt and response, typical concurrency, peak TPS?
[00:04:02] Priya: Average prompt ~120 tokens, typical response ~60 tokens, but for product details we sometimes request up to 400 tokens. Concurrency on typical day 15 rps, peak 120 rps during flash sales. But many calls are short (few tokens) and many are cached at prefix. We can provide real traces.

[00:05:30] Alex: Okay, for sizing we'll use three buckets—chat short (<=200 tokens), detail (200-500 tokens), long/fulfillment (500+). For the pilot let's target reproducing peak pattern at 50% of peak (so ~60 rps) to validate scaling and latency. Does that sound reasonable?
[00:05:48] Jordan: Yes, start smaller is fine.

[00:06:30] Samir: On benchmarks—recommended we capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec variance, cost per 1k tokens, and accuracy for structured outputs via a labeled prompt set. We'll provide a benchmark harness script that can replay customer logs and run mixed workloads.

[00:07:10] Priya: For accuracy we need to assert intent extraction F1 > 0.88 on our labeled set, and structured JSON must validate against our schema with <2% parsing errors. Is Redwood able to run evals and host metrics dashboards for that?
[00:07:28] Samir: Yes, Redwood Console can ingest eval results and we'll wire the labeled set. We'll also surface token-level cost and per-route latency. Small caveat: if you use Dedicated vs Hosted we can show more stable p95s—Dedicated gives predictable throughput but costs more.

[00:08:40] Jordan: We are leaning Hosted for faster onboarding, but we need VPC or private deployment for PCI scope later. How disruptive is switching from Hosted pilot to Private later?
[00:08:58] Alex: The API and SDK are the same across modes. Migration is primarily networking and key management. We recommend starting Hosted with stricter data retention, then move to Dedicated or Private for production. We'll document the migration checklist.

[00:10:15] Marcus: On KMS: we require customer-managed keys for any production PII tokens. Does Redwood support external KMS/HSM integrations in Private?
[00:10:27] Samir: Yes, Private and Dedicated integrate with customer KMS. Hosted supports envelope encryption but if you need HSM and full control that's Private.

[00:11:50] Priya: Tool calling—our flow: model should return a structured intent JSON with fields: intent, entities[], confidence, and optionally a tool invocation spec when action required (e.g., checkOrder(order_id)). We also want a canonical function signature for the platform to call.
[00:12:12] Samir: Two integration patterns: 1) OpenAI-compatible function calling—model returns a function call and Redwood will forward that via SDK; 2) SDK-based richer primitives with typed bindings and retries. For pilot we can support both; we'll map function schema to your runtime and provide a sample middleware.

[00:13:00] Jordan: We also need step-by-step deterministic outputs for downstream parsers. OpenAI-style function calling can be flaky with hallucinated args sometimes. How does Redwood mitigate that?
[00:13:18] Samir: Mitigations: structured output schemas with strict validation, token-level sampling controls, and a small verification rerank step where a lightweight rule model checks JSON before invoking tools. Also you can set deterministic decoding and temperature=0 for critical calls.

[00:14:40] Priya: Do you support streaming partial structured outputs? We want to stream token-by-token to UX while also accumulating JSON.
[00:14:53] Samir: We support streaming and can emit partial JSON blobs, but for validation we'll prefer full JSON at end. We'll demo streaming + post-validate in the pilot.

[00:16:05] Alex: Let's talk OpenAI-compat endpoints vs SDK—tradeoffs: OpenAI-compat is minimal change if you already have code calling OpenAI, but SDK gives more control (batching, retries, built-in function-mapping, better telemetry). Recommend SDK for pilot if you want the observability.

[00:17:02] Jordan: Our frontend already uses OpenAI-style calls. Time to market matters so OpenAI-compat bridge might be easiest initially.

[00:17:25] Samir: Fine—pilot plan: we can ship both: give you an OpenAI-compat endpoint to swap in quickly, and parallel SDK integration for deeper telemetry. We'll run benchmark traffic to both and compare latency/cost.

[00:18:50] Priya: For benchmarks, can Redwood emulate prefix KV cache to measure cache hit benefits?
[00:19:02] Samir: Yes, Redwood runtime supports KV cache and we can configure cache warmth in harness. We'll show baseline without cache, and then with cache warmed with realistic prefixes.

[00:20:44] Jordan: Success criteria recap—latency p50 <400ms, p95 <800ms under pilot load, intent F1 >0.88, structured parse error <2%, and cost target—Redwood to propose. Also stability during 30-minute continuous load at 60 rps.

[00:21:35] Alex: Good. Timeline—4-week pilot. Week 0 (this week): share runbook, access, and sample logs. Week 1: Redwood spins up eval account + seed models, customer runs harness. Week 2: joint benchmark, iterate function schema. Week 3: refine quality and run 2-hour sustained run. Week 4: final report and decision (go/no-go). Is that doable for you?
[00:21:59] Jordan: Yes, that fits. We have a leadership check-in end of month.

[00:23:10] Marcus: Networking—we'll need an IP allowlist and short-lived certs. For hosted, can you do IP allowlist and mTLS?
[00:23:24] Samir: Hosted supports IP allowlist and token auth; mTLS is supported on Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we can accept a limited allowlist plus SSO for dashboard.

[00:24:40] Priya: One thing—can Redwood's Console export audit logs in a format we can ingest to Splunk? Our security team will ask.
[00:24:52] Alex: Yes, audit logs can be exported to S3 and consumed by Splunk via S3 ingestion. We'll include sample format.

[00:25:55] Jordan: Are there any gotchas with OpenAI-compat APIs—like slightly different parameter names or behavior?
[00:26:05] Samir: There are small differences; function calling semantics are largely compatible but edge cases exist (e.g., content-type handling, multipart streams). We'll send a compatibility matrix.

[00:27:40] Priya: For evaluation, we need deterministic reproduction—can the harness snapshot seeds and RNG states so we repeat runs?
[00:27:50] Samir: Yes, harness supports deterministic seeds; we can also pin model versions in Redwood to ensure consistent runs.

[00:29:00] Jordan: On model variants—we want to compare a smaller quantized model vs larger baseline for cost/latency tradeoffs. Can you recommend quantization profiles?
[00:29:12] Samir: We'll propose three profiles: fast-quant (8-bit with optimized kernels), balanced (mixed-precision), and high-fidelity. We'll provide benchmark numbers on your token mix.

[00:30:25] Alex: Ok, let's capture action items and owners—Samir will send harness, Alex sends runbook and pricing, Priya sends logs, Marcus confirms VPC/KMS, and we'll meet for deep-dive next Tues.

[00:31:00] Jordan: Quick Q—what telemetry will you surface per-request? We need request_id, model_version, tokens_in/out, latency, cache_hit boolean.
[00:31:12] Samir: All of those plus routing policy, host node id, and cost estimate. We'll show sample dashboard.

[00:33:10] Priya: Regarding function calling, can we add a verification step where the model returns both a function call and a natural language explanation for auditing?
[00:33:25] Samir: Yes, you can request additional 'explain' field; cost/latency tradeoff, but fine for audit logs.

[00:34:40] Marcus: Security checklist items from our side: SOC2 report review, SSO/SAML for console, RBAC for keys, and encryption in transit at rest. We'll need Redwood's attestation docs.
[00:35:00] Alex: We'll attach SOC2 type II report, SAML setup guide and an architecture doc for KMS flows.

[00:36:20] Jordan: Any blockers we've missed?
[00:36:24] Priya: None from ML—just need logs and schema.
[00:36:30] Marcus: I'll check networking but expect minor config.

[00:37:05] Samir: One last operational note: for pilot we recommend throttles and automatic fallback to a smaller model when latency climbs—we can configure routing policies to do that.
[00:37:22] Jordan: Fallback behavior—if we fall back to smaller model, we need an SLA on correctness drop and a feature flag to switch it off for certain routes.
[00:37:34] Samir: We'll surface per-route fallback toggles in the Console, and a canary policy for rollout.

[00:38:50] Alex: Recap of next steps and deliverables—see action items. We'll send calendar invite for the technical deep-dive next Tuesday 16:00 UTC.
[00:39:10] Jordan: Thanks everyone—looking forward to the runbook.

[00:39:20] Priya: Thanks.
[00:39:22] Marcus: Thanks all.

Caveats / transcription notes: occasional overlap, "Redwood Console" transcribed as "Redwood Console" mostly correct; some product names may be slightly off in spots (e.g., 'KV cache' heard as 'K V cash' once).

End of transcript.
